llmTip: CRITICAL: When searching emails, the $search parameter value MUST follow the following format: $search="your search query here". When using the $search parameter, don't use the $orderby parameter. Use KQL (Keyword Query Language) syntax to search specific properties: 'from:', 'subject:', 'body:', 'to:', 'cc:', 'bcc:', 'attachment:', 'hasAttachments:', 'importance:', 'received:', 'sent:'. Examples: $search="from:john@example.com" | $search="subject:meeting AND hasAttachments:true" | $search="body:urgent AND received>=2024-01-01" | $search="from:john AND importance:high". Remember: ALWAYS wrap the entire search expression in double quotes! Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/search-query-parameter IMPORTANT: Always use $select to limit returned fields and reduce response size. Recommended default: $select=id,subject,from,toRecipients,receivedDateTime,bodyPreview,isRead,hasAttachments. Use bodyPreview instead of body for listings. To read the full email body, use get-mail-message with the specific message id. WORKFLOW RULE: If the user asks to draft/reply/forward the latest email, first use this tool to get the message id, then MUST call the corresponding draft tool (create-reply-draft, create-reply-all-draft, create-forward-draft, etc.).

Use this exact tool when the user asks for Outlook categories, Outlook tags, mail categories, colored labels, or the master category list. It lists the user's Outlook categories (colored labels) used to tag messages, events, contacts, and tasks. Do not use list-mail-folders for categories/tags. Use update-mail-message with body { "categories": ["Category Name"] } to apply categories to an email.

Creates a new Outlook category/tag. Always include a visible color preset so Outlook clients display it reliably. Body: { "displayName": "Category Name", "color": "preset0" }. Do not use color "None" unless the user explicitly asks for no color. Category names are case-sensitive when applied to messages.

Updates an existing Outlook category/tag. Microsoft Graph only allows changing the color, not renaming the displayName. Body: { "color": "preset0" }. Use list-outlook-categories first to find the category id. Do not use color "None" unless the user explicitly asks for no color.

Deletes an Outlook category/tag from the user's master category list. Use list-outlook-categories first to find the category id. Deleting a category does not automatically remove that category string from items that already have it assigned; update affected messages/events separately if cleanup is required.
Lists mail folders only. Do not use this for Outlook categories, tags, colored labels, or the master category list; use list-outlook-categories instead.
Creates a top-level mail folder. Use create-mail-child-folder to create a subfolder inside an existing folder. Use list-mail-folders to find existing folder IDs.
Creates a subfolder inside an existing mail folder. Use list-mail-folders or list-mail-child-folders to find the parent folder ID.
Renames a mail folder by updating its displayName. Use list-mail-folders to find the folder ID.

Updates properties on an existing Outlook email. To tag an email, patch categories with body { "categories": ["Category Name"] }. Graph replaces the full categories array, so read existing categories first when adding or removing a single category.

CRITICAL: Use this tool when the user asks to draft (not send) a forward of an existing email. Provide the message id and put generated text in body.Message.body.content as HTML or plain text; the MCP creates the real Outlook forward draft first and prepends your generated content above the quoted forwarded history. Preserve recipients in Message.toRecipients or ToRecipients. Do NOT use create-draft-email for forwards of existing messages. Do NOT output only a manual draft template.

CRITICAL: Use this tool when the user asks to draft (not send) a reply to an existing email. First fetch the message id, then call create-reply-draft with generated text in body.Message.body.content as HTML or plain text; the MCP creates the real Outlook reply draft first and prepends your generated content above the quoted thread history. Do NOT use create-draft-email for replies to existing messages. Do NOT manually fake Re: subjects. Do NOT output only a manual draft template.

CRITICAL: Use this tool when the user asks to draft (not send) a reply-all to an existing email. First fetch the message id, then call create-reply-all-draft with generated text in body.Message.body.content as HTML or plain text; the MCP creates the real Outlook reply-all draft first and prepends your generated content above the quoted thread history. Do NOT use create-draft-email for replies to existing messages. Do NOT manually fake Re: subjects. Do NOT output only a manual draft template.

Returns expanded recurring event instances (not just seriesMaster) within a date range for the default calendar. Requires startDateTime and endDateTime query parameters in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z). Use get-specific-calendar-view if you need a non-default calendar. To find Teams meetings, use $filter=isOnlineMeeting eq true. To search by subject, use $filter=contains(subject,'keyword'). Teams meetings include a joinWebUrl property needed for transcript access via list-online-meetings.

Returns expanded recurring event instances (not just seriesMaster) within a date range for a specific calendar. Requires startDateTime and endDateTime query parameters in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z). Each instance includes seriesMasterId and type (occurrence/exception) fields for recurring event linkage. Use fetchAllPages=true to retrieve all results when there are many events. To find Teams meetings, use $filter=isOnlineMeeting eq true. Teams meetings include a joinWebUrl property needed for transcript access via list-online-meetings.

Expand a recurring event into individual instances within a date range. Requires startDateTime and endDateTime query parameters in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z). Use this to see all occurrences of a recurring event.
